history.summary: 12th-century temple complex about 2 km northeast of Latur city at Hatte Nagar, dedicated to Siddharameshwar of Solapur - the 12th-century Veerashaiva saint, poet in Kannada and participant in Basavanna's Veerashaiva movement. Tradition holds it was built by King Tamradwaj, a devotee of Siddharameshwar, and it is the Gram Daivat (presiding deity) of Latur. The complex has intricate carvings of mythological figures and additional shrines of Ramlingeswar, Bhuteswar, Keshavraj, Ram and Dutta. The main shrine is ancient; the large sabhamandap is a 1988 addition (cement concrete, 18 pillars, seats ~3,000, used for marriages), with about 52 pilgrim cloisters along the fortification wall and a sacred teertha beyond the southern gate. A large annual fair runs for about 10 days from Mahashivratri and is among Latur's biggest religious gatherings. name: Siddheshwar Ratneshwar Mandir
town_description: Latur is a city in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, known as a regional education hub and part of the state's sugar belt. Its landmarks include the 12th-century Siddheshwar Ratneshwar temple complex and the 1917 Ganj Golai market, where 15 streets converge on a central roundabout housing the Devi Jagdamba temple. The district was devastated by the 1993 Killari earthquake, after which much of the city was rebuilt.
